source.title: Effective Federated Adaptive Gradient Methods with Non-IID Decentralized Data
source.authors: Qianqian Tong; Guannan Liang; J. Bi

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendix are present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: Compares federated adaptive optimizers with other federated methods on image-classification tasks and reports test accuracy, extending optimizer comparisons to non-IID decentralized training.
record.gate_note: The study reports training loss and test accuracy, including a numerical MNIST comparison and plotted CIFAR results. Its adaptive-optimizer comparisons bear on V4, but it does not report train-to-test gaps or test the other claim versions. Cited results from other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out image-classification accuracy under adaptive server updates versus FedAvg and FedMomentum in federated learning. This bears on V4 in a new setting, although its tuning includes momentum and calibration parameters beyond learning rates and schedules.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that carefully calibrated federated adaptive methods converge faster and are less prone to bad local minima, and report improved test performance with calibration and stage-wise local learning-rate decay. They do not demonstrate a generalization-gap mechanism independent of optimization performance.
record.recipe_differences: Federated optimization with local SGD updates and adaptive server-side updates on non-IID decentralized data; compares federated algorithms rather than standard centralized optimizer recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Test performance varies with calibration scheme and its parameters, non-IID level, local update count, and learning-rate schedule; the text also reports a later-stage decline for FedAdam.

fits_no_version.finding: Calibration-dependent convergence bounds and gradient-norm behavior concern optimization stationarity; the sharp-minimum discussion does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Calibration parameters affect convergence and optimization behavior in federated adaptive methods.

record.problems: The MNIST table reports means with ± values but does not define those uncertainty terms in the supplied text. CIFAR outcomes are mostly plots without numerical values in the text. The study does not report train-to-test gaps, so its results do not directly measure generalization gaps.
record.rows_left_out: Other Table 2 entries for FedAMSGrad, calibrated methods and K values were not extracted; the kept rows cover the principal FedAdam versus FedAvg/FedMomentum comparison at each K. Figure-only method-specific comparisons in Figures 2–5 and appendix Figures 7–13 were not separately extracted where the text does not give an explicit result for the claim's comparison.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Centralized optimizer comparisons; tuning restricted to learning rates and schedules; worse held-out performance despite matched or better training performance; language benchmarks; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and rankings against norm or margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: A separate row for the explicit finding that s-FedAMSGrad consistently achieves the highest CIFAR100 test accuracy. Record VGGNet and the stated federated conditions, rather than assigning ResNet-20 as in R7.
missing.locator: Section 4.4; comparison context in Figure 3(d–f), with S=10 and K=10 stated in Section 4.4

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. All clients use local SGD; adaptivity is applied at the server. Section 4.1 explicitly tunes momentum and algorithm-specific parameters, so the MNIST results should not be presented as contradictions of the limited-tuning clause. Figure curves cannot be reconstructed from the supplied text alone.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image networks.

The study tests federated adaptive methods on image classification, but does not compare standard non-federated optimizers, language benchmarks, or explicitly isolate limited tuning, equal training performance, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, or word-level language models.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Non-IID MNIST, S=30, K=10 or 50, with momentum parameters and learning rates tuned
relationships.reason: R3–R4 show FedAdam outperforming FedAvg/FedMomentum: 98.57 versus 97.22/96.79 and 98.10 versus 97.67/97.74. This qualifies the adaptive-method disadvantage in this federated, broader-tuning setting.
relationships.display_finding: FedAdam reportedly outperformed FedAvg and FedMomentum, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.reason: R5 shows essentially equal accuracies: FedAdam 97.59, FedAvg 97.56 and FedMomentum 97.57, with reported uncertainties larger than the differences.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracies were close relative to their uncertainties, but the comparison remains unverified.
